questions.prompt: Which month opens the season of spring?
questions.explanation: Spring is made of March, April and May, and the first of the three is March. April and May follow it, and February is still the last month of winter.

questions.prompt: It is snowy and very cold outside. What do you put on your hands before you go out?
questions.explanation: Gloves are the winter clothes made for the hands. Socks and boots keep the feet warm, and a sweater covers the body, so none of the three protects your hands from the cold.

questions.prompt: There is fog on the road and you cannot see the houses. Complete: "It is a ___ morning."
questions.explanation: The adjective is the noun plus a y, and fog is consonant plus vowel plus consonant, so the g is doubled: foggy. The noun fog names the thing in the air, the spelling with one g forgets the doubling, and the -ing form names an action.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Next winter we ___ swim in the sea, because the water ___ be very cold."
questions.explanation: Nobody swims in a very cold sea, so the first blank says what will not happen and takes won't; the second blank says what the water will really be, so it takes will. Giving both blanks the same word makes the sentence contradict its own because.

questions.prompt: Which sentence compares two seasons correctly?

options.text: Spring is more warm than winter.

questions.explanation: Warm is a short adjective, so it takes -er and the second season comes after than: Spring is warmer than winter. English keeps more for long adjectives, the bare adjective cannot stand in front of than, and the word after the comparison is never that.

questions.prompt: Complete the list of spring activities: "catching butterflies, ___ flowers, walking outside."
questions.explanation: The list names activities, and an activity is the verb plus -ing: collecting flowers, just like catching and walking beside it. The bare verb, the form with to and the form with -s all name the action but none of them names the activity.
